extracted.intended_audience: authors, journal and book editors, copyeditors, proofreaders, indexers, and production staff in publishing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for preparing, editing, and producing scholarly and trade manuscripts (books, chapters, journal articles, illustrations, indexes, and front/back matter). Covers orthography, punctuation, citations, figures/tables, permissions, and production conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and categories for when to use capitalization across many classes of words and names (proper nouns generally; sparing use of “down style”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment for groups of people (ethnic/national groups, generations, physical characteristics, sexual orientation and gender identity, socioeconomic classes); historical and cultural terminology (acts, treaties, government programs, awards, cultural movements, events, oaths and pledges, periods); personifications; place-names (cities, towns, compass points, continents, countries, political divisions, popular names, public places, regions, topographical divisions, urban areas); religious terms (deities, events/concepts, groups, names/titles, objects, places of worship, figures, works); scientific/technical terminology (abbreviations, astronomical, botanical/zoological, genetic, geological, medical, physical/chemical); titles and offices; quotations and questions within sentences; propernouns generally; and guidance to use 'down style' sparingly (8.1). Numerous cross-references to section numbers (e.g., 8.37, 8.45–8.111).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital letters (uses and formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: When to use full-size capital letters and special uses of capitals in text and display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses include compass points in addresses, drop caps/initials, full-size for emphasis (preferred to small caps), for generations, keyboard combinations/shortcuts, musical elements, plurals of letters, scholastic letter grades, standing for names, and when letters are used as words. See also small caps and all-caps formatting; punctuation and pluralization rules for letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caps and small caps format
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the use and preference between full-size capitals and small caps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full-size capitals are preferred to small caps for emphasis (7.52, 9.34, 10.8, 10.38). Rules on plural forms, use in indexes, and in legal-style citations also noted. See related sections on caps, small caps, and all-caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intercaps (midcaps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of interpunctional capital letters in compound names and brand styling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a separate consideration (8.154) — consult when encountering midcap/joined capitalization in organization or product names and when deciding preservation vs. standardization in text and indexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captions for illustrations and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for writing and formatting captions (defined, syntax, punctuation, labeling, and proofreading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captions are defined and discussed (3.7, 3.21–28). Guidance covers accessibility issues (3.28), capitalization in captions (3.21, 3.22), separation of illustration number from caption (3.23, 6.120), punctuation in captions (3.21, 3.23, 3.24, 6.14), syntax, titles of works in captions, locators for parts of illustrations, credit lines, original dimensions, proofreading of captions (2.113), examples (figs. 3.1, 3.4–9), captions for charts and musical examples, and special handling for illustrations with parts (3.12). Also notes electronic supplementary-data mentions in captions (3.26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Charts and graphs (use and preparation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate use, definition, and production requirements for charts and graphs as alternatives to tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice includes appropriate use and definition (3.41), axes and curves (3.43, 3.52), consistency (2.65, 3.42), credit lines for commissioned work (3.33), electronic-file preparation (3.43), examples (figs. 3.8–10), genealogical/pedigree charts (3.46), indexing of charts (16.116), labels (3.44, 3.45), line art considerations (3.4, 3.41), symbol/pattern choices (3.25), and titles of charts (3.44).

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript and editorial concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational standards for manuscript handling, submission, cross-checking, editing, and proofreading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes cross-checking, editing workflow, guidelines for authors, proofreading, separate files for illustrations, submission procedures, working numbers, marking proofs and manuscripts for punctuation or style changes, designers' alterations (DAs), content proofing (2.32, 2.65, 2.3, 2.26, 2.37, 2.115, 2.28, 2.91, 2.134, 2.135, 2.140).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes and index creation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for index entries, checking, cross-references, main headings and subentries, locators, column handling, and continued lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers checking and editing indexes (16.126, 16.130, 16.133), cross-references (16.15–23), alphabetizing rules (16.58–93), placement and punctuation of cross-references (16.17–20, 16.23), blind cross-refs (16.16), generic vs. specific entries (16.23), inlists and columns for indexes (1.39, 16.24, 16.135), locators and continued lines (16.111, 16.139), indentation/running styles, use of italics, overuse of cross-references, use of dedicated indexing software (16.104), and indexing of various forms of names (personal, corporate, place-names) with language-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references in text and citations
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format, check, and use cross-references within running text and source citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes alterations to cross-references (2.136), use in electronic publications (1.120–121), cross-references for illustrations (2.28), in-text citational cross-references to chapters/sections (2.35, 8.180), and handling of 'see'/'see also' forms (16.16–20, 16.26, 16.96).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source citations (general rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for preparing source citations across formats (author-date, legal-style, journal/article/chapter/book, DOIs and URLs, access dates, and special-source types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses author-date reference system, DOIs (14.8, 14.161), URLs and DOIs in text (14.17), blog comments, newspaper headlines, magazine departments, publishers' names, titles of works, classical Greek/Latin works, legal-style citations (14.272–290), magazine/newspaper/journal citation formats, shortened citations, examples and variations, access-date treatment, databases and accession numbers, multimedia content (recording/performance dates), and examples across sections (14.xx, 15.xx).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation management software and databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of bibliographic databases and citation management tools in preparing citations and metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes citation-management software (14.5, 14.12), bibliographic databases (14.67), metadata in databases (1.75, 1.92, 1.121), permalinks/DOIs, and interaction with publisher databases (14.9–14.11, 14.161, 14.164, 14.175).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright (law and practical handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive rules and considerations regarding copyright, registration, duration, rights, permissions, and publisher/author responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers accuracy/candor in process, assignment/licensing, authorship rights and varieties, works made for hire, duration (life plus seventy, table 4.1), electronic publications, fair use, importance of registration, deposit requirements, dual systems, public display, preregistration, benefits of registering, renewal, renewal exceptions for older works, non-US publications, open-access models, photocopying and permissions, publisher responsibilities for copyright, 'reasonable effort' to correct mistakes, termination of transfers, and symbol/wording and examples for notices. See major sections 4.1–4.99 and page references for notices and pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright notice and copyright page contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Required components and placement of the copyright notice and the typical elements of a copyright page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Components include copyright notice, ISBN, DOI and DOI metadata, publisher's address, country of printing, publication date, imprint/edition details, CIP data, ISBN/ISSN, illustration credits, grant information, permissions, impression line, paper durability statement, and proofing items (1.20, 1.22, 1.23, 1.24, figs. 1.1–1.4). Guidance on mistakes, placement, renewal, and inclusion in notes and journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Commons and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how to use Creative Commons licenses and related open licenses for content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References use of Creative Commons (3.32, 3.34, 4.52, 4.60, 4.62) and interactions with publisher permissions and electronic rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions, compilations, and previously published material
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of compilations/collected works and permissions requirements for previously published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses compilations of previously published material (2.43–47), permissions responsibilities, permissible changes to previously published material (2.44, 2.61), illustration inclusion (2.47), notes and source notes (1.50, 2.46, 14.54), and implications for copyrights and publishing agreements (4.5, 4.10, 4.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Color in reproduction and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for using color in illustrations, proofs, line art, and electronic supplementary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes color in illustrations (1.6, 2.37, 3.3, 3.15, 3.19, 3.43), process printing, color proofs (prepress), color separation, color in line art, color for journal covers, and handling of color in marking manuscripts and proofs (2.93, 2.132). Also mentions color and accessibility concerns and marking changes for tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and tabular material
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting, referencing, and layout standards for tables including continued lines and inlist treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers tables (3.54–3.59, 3.60, 3.77–3.87), use of tables vs. charts (3.48), text references to illustrations and tables (3.50), cut-in heads and table placement (3.53, 3.58), continued lines in tables (3.86–87), locators for parts of illustrations, table titles and source notes, use in index and running heads, and proofreading of tables (2.31, 3.77).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commas (punctuation rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive guidance on comma usage in multiple syntactic and citation contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics include commas with abbreviations (academic/professional designations, Inc., Jr.), with clauses (compound, dependent, independent, relative), serial/Oxford comma (6.19–21), uses in source citations (access dates, authors, magazine/newspaper conventions), in lists and parenthetical elements, and when to omit commas. Cross-references to sections on semicolons, colons, parentheses, and quotation punctuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colons (uses and spacing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for when to use colons, capitalization after colons, spacing, and interactions with other punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses include introducing lists, non-English language conventions, with dates in titles of works, direct address, double/multiple numeration, glossaries, indexes, tables, with quotations or speech, ratios, scriptural citations, and between titles and subtitles. Notes on spacing, capitalization following colons, em-dash substitutions, and marking for manuscripts and proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashes (types and usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on em dashes, en dashes, 2-em dashes, marking manuscripts for dashes, and when to use which dash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses length comparisons, 2-em dashes (usage and marking), typing and manuscript marking (2.96), difference vs. parentheses, 3-em dashes, and related punctuation choices (6.75, 6.93, 13.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates (formats and usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred date formats, avoiding ambiguity, inclusive dates, treatment in citations and legal-style references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formats discussed include day-month-year, month-day-year, year-month-day (ISO), all-numeral styles; handling of decades and centuries; punctuation (commas, en dashes, slashes); access dates in citations; fiscal years; incomplete dates; holidays; and special guidance for legal-style citations (acts, bills, hearings) and for titles of works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound terms and hyphenation
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on hyphenation and formation of compound terms (open, closed, suspended), and when to use en dash vs. hyphen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers closed vs. open compounds, hyphenation of compound modifiers, compound adverbs, suspended hyphens, en dash versus hyphen rules (6.80–81), personal names in compounds, ethnic groups/nationalities, trend toward closed compounds, and a hyphenation guide (7.81–89).

rubrics_metrics.name: Company and organization names
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for capitalization, abbreviations, ampersand use, alphabetizing, possessives, and indexing of company/organization names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes handling of Inc./Ltd. abbreviations, articles in names, ampersands in names, unusual capitalization (e.g., eBay), omissible parts, spelling out in running text, possessives, alphabetizing in indexes, and capitalization (8.62–70, 10.23–26, 14.133–136, 16.89).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapters and chapter titles (display and metadata)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting of chapters including numbering, display, chapter titles, abstracting, endnotes, bibliographies, pagination, running heads, and proofing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on chapter display (1.8, 1.12, 1.16, 1.37, 1.46), chapter numbers and numeration across parts, chapters as individual works in multivolume works, abstracts for chapters, appendixes at end of chapters, bibliographies/reference lists per chapter, running heads, pagination, multiple author chapters, editing and proofreading of chapter titles, punctuation after titles (no punctuation following), and table-of-contents placement and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names, personal and place (capitalization, alphabetizing)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to treat personal names, particles, married names, transliteration, and place-names in text and in indexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes alphabetizing personal names (16.72–93), particles (da, de, etc.), married women's names, Portuguese/Spanish name conventions, transliteration for Chinese/Cyrillic/Russian, English forms of non-English city names, capitalization rules for place-names, handling 'Fort/Mount/Saint' in names, and indexing considerations for non-English names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and public documents (citations and naming)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment and citation of laws, treaties, constitutions, court decisions, and legislative materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers legal-style citations (14.272–290), citations for constitutions and amendments, acts/treaties, bills/resolutions, hearings, international entities, and jurisdiction-specific guidance for US federal, state/local, UK, Canadian, and international courts and records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation with quotations and titles
rubrics_metrics.description: How to punctuate quotations within text, quoted titles, questions within sentences, and punctuation interacting with quotation marks and titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes punctuation around quotations (13.xx, 6.9–6.10), placement of commas/periods with quotation marks, question marks/exclamation points within or outside quotes depending on scope, punctuation in titles of works within text and in source citations, and handling of quoted titles in captions and indexes (8.162, 13.18–21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and marking conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for proofreading manuscripts, marking proofs, and content proof responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers proofreader's marks, marking manuscripts for commas/colons/dashes, proofreading captions/tables/chapters/copyright pages, content proof (2.140), and use of designers' alterations (DAs), tracking changes, and editorial/interpolations. Also references to proofreading of running heads and front/back matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer and technical terminology (capitalization and forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling of computer/software-related terms, abbreviations, fonts, and interface elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes capitalization and fonts for application names, keyboard combos and shortcuts, abbreviations for apps/devices/OS, binary system notation, resources, and application-specific variations (7.76–80). Also mentions CSS and electronic publication style issues (p.978, 1.107).
